key_insight: FUSE shows you can substantially improve verification accuracy by unsupervisedly ensembling multiple imperfect verifiers (LLM judges, reward models) without any ground-truth correctness labels, extracting a more reliable consensus signal from noisy scorers.
problem_solved: How to verify and rank LLM outputs when obtaining ground-truth correctness labels is costly or impossible and available verifiers (human-like judges, reward models) are noisy and imperfect.
method: Aggregate diverse verifier scores (e.g., LLM judges, reward models) for each candidate output to form a multi-view scoring matrix.
Apply a label-free ensembling/aggregation procedure that calibrates weights, detects outliers, and extracts a consensus ranking or score without access to ground-truth labels.
Iteratively refine ensemble weights and consensus (e.g., via agreement-based weighting or consistency checks) to boost verifier reliability.
impact: Enables higher-quality verification and selection of model outputs without expensive labeled data, reducing cost and improving safety/utility for training (e.g., RLHF) and deployment of LLM systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (candidate outputs) → multiple verifiers (icons) → unsupervised ensembling module → consensus score/ranking
Bar chart: ensemble performance vs individual verifiers (accuracy/precision metrics) showing ensemble gains
Heatmap or network of pairwise verifier agreement to visualize which verifiers align and which are outliers
Flowchart showing iterative weight update / outlier detection steps in the unsupervised aggregation
paper_title: FUSE: Ensembling Verifiers with Zero Labeled Data
paper_authors: Joonhyuk Lee, Virginia Ma, Sarah Zhao, Yash Nair, Asher Spector
